solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sound surprised when shortlist's brought in edited

indicators.note: one piece is brought in, so it goes inside the other
short means the word before it loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before being cut short

indicators.note: something edited has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shortlist has been edited, and someone gives a low whistle of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortlist' must be split in two: 'short' trims the word before it, and 'edited' works on 'list'; 'brought in' sets one inside the other. The 's stands for 'is' and is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People whistle as a reaction when they are surprised or impressed, so the verb fits the phrase.

clue.text: Australian baby carrier's top grade model

parts.note: the womb is where a baby is carried before birth
A is the highest grade in exams
the Model T was the classic Ford car

explanation.surface: A first-rate pram or pouch for an Aussie baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby carrier' looks like a pouch or pram but is the WOMB; the model is Ford's Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing marsupial native to Australia, so it is a typical Australian animal.

clue.text: Weak drug's key in hospitals for chronic condition

parts.note: ill can mean weak or poorly

indicators.note: the drug and key letters sit inside the two hospital letters

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital, so two give HH
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A frail patient's medication is key to hospital care for a long illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'hospitals' supplies two letters, one per hospital, which 'in' splits around the drug and key.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill health is a lasting state of poor wellbeing, the kind of chronic condition that persists.

clue.text: Keep an eye on circling river current

indicators.note: the tending word circles round the river letter

parts.note: to tend is to look after
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone watches a river that has a swirling current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like the river's flow, but it is the noun meaning a prevailing tendency.
explanation.definitionFit: A current of opinion is a general drift or direction, which is what a trend is.

clue.text: Leave bright and early, beginning ahead of fair

indicators.note: the opening letter is put before the other pieces
only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: to quit is to leave
an able pupil is a bright one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a fair bright and early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a fete to leave, but it is the adjective meaning just.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means just and even-handed, which is what fair means in this sense.

clue.text: Take so long repressing iron on fine silk

indicators.note: to repress is to hold down inside, so the farewell word keeps the other pieces within it

parts.note: TA-TA is a casual way of saying goodbye

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone takes ages pressing fine silk with an iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is just the instruction to begin. 'repressing' looks like ironing language, but it means the farewell holds the other letters down inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric traditionally made from silk.

clue.text: Attempts taking boy away from gangs

indicators.note: taking with away from means one letter is removed from the other word
together with taking, the boy's letter leaves the gangs word

parts.note: tribes are groups, loosely gangs
B is used for boy, though few dictionaries list it

explanation.surface: Efforts to pull a young lad away from street gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIBES loses B. B for boy is rare: the blog found it in none of three dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Tries are attempts, as in having a try at something.

clue.text: Eat last bit of fish fin stew

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone eats the last of a fish-fin stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the dish but rearranges OF FISH FIN; the definition borrows only 'Eat last bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish off a meal is to eat the final portion of it, polishing it off.

clue.text: Mike has trouble with partner over online message

indicators.note: in a down clue the partner letter sits over the rest

parts.note: in bridge, East is partner to West, giving E
Mike is the NATO phonetic-alphabet word for M
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Mike has problems with his partner over a message sent online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partner' comes from bridge, where the four players sit as North, South, East and West in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is a message sent electronically over the internet.

clue.text: Finding out when Family Guy's starting

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
kin are family members

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: A viewer asks when the cartoon Family Guy starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family Guy' looks like the TV show title but splits: Family gives KIN, Guy's start gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is how one finds out, so the action and its purpose coincide as a loose synonym.

clue.text: Feel embittered amid rampant confusion

indicators.note: in heraldry a rampant beast rears up, so in this down-reading sense the letters are turned backwards
amid means the letters are found inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Someone feels embittered while surrounded by widespread confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' picks EELEM out of 'fEEL EMbittered'; 'rampant' (rearing up) turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused scuffle or jumble, so it is a scene of confusion.

clue.text: Sailor's association moved forward with standard for use at sea

indicators.note: the second word of the pair is moved to the front

parts.note: Jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor
a union is an association of workers or members

explanation.surface: A sailors' union steps forward with a flag for seafaring use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved forward' makes JACK UNION into UNION JACK. Pedants note the name strictly applies to the jack flown at a ship's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the Union Jack is the British flag flown as a jack on naval ships.

clue.text: Noted case solved with personal testimonies

indicators.note: a case that is solved has been worked out, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous criminal case is cracked thanks to witness statements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' rearranges the ten letters of NOTED CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotes are short personal accounts of things the teller has experienced, a kind of informal testimony.

clue.text: Half of girls in review love new hair studio

indicators.note: to review is to look back, so the half-word is read backwards
only the first half of the six-letter word is taken

parts.note: lasses are girls, mainly in northern English and Scottish use
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A girls' magazine review gives a new hairdresser's a glowing write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girls' is LASSES; 'Half of' gives LAS, and 'in review' turns that to SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a hairdresser's premises, where hair is styled and treated.

clue.text: Look after fellow priest in Turkey

indicators.note: the word for look comes after the fellow's letter

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone cares for a priest friend living in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the country, but it is a failure: a turkey is a show that bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: In show business a turkey is a production that fails badly, just as a flop does.

clue.text: Fine china with intricate pelican drawn in gold

indicators.note: the gold letters are drawn inside the jumbled bird
something intricate is involved and tangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Delicate china decorated with an elaborate pelican picked out in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intricate' turns the bird into PCELAIN, and 'drawn in' sets the heraldic gold inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is the fine translucent ceramic called china.

clue.text: Tiresome person endlessly argued and scrounged

indicators.note: without its end, so the word drops its last letter

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
to row is to quarrel noisily

explanation.surface: A tedious person kept arguing and cadged things off others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BORE to BOR. ROWED rhymes with 'cowed', meaning quarrelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to get something by cadging, and borrowing without real intent to repay is the same idea.

clue.text: Organise support around huge redwood, finally past its best

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it

indicators.note: the support word goes around the huge letters

parts.note: a tee supports the ball in golf
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Arrange props round a giant redwood that is finally in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is the golf TEE, holding OS (outsize).
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has run to seed has stopped producing and gone straggly, so it is past its best.

clue.text: Testing questions for former American politician reap storm

parts.note: ex means former
MP stands for Member of Parliament

indicators.note: to storm is to rage about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An ex-politician from America faces tough questions and reaps a storm of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges REAP to PAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam paper is the printed set of questions that tests candidates.

clue.text: Unlucky number have seven deducted from score

definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, and twenty minus seven is ...

explanation.surface: A sportsman docked seven points ends up with an unlucky total.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is arithmetic, not letter work: a score is twenty, less seven leaves thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstition holds that thirteen brings bad luck, hence fear of Friday the 13th.

clue.text: Crop's cut in America after fall ends

indicators.note: the cutting word follows the end letters
only the two end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe, to chop

explanation.surface: A harvest is cut down in America after autumn arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' looks like the American autumn but only gives its ends, FL. 'Crop's' is 'Crop is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is a plant grown as a field crop for its fibre, used for linen, and its seed.

clue.text: Ghastly puce cover for horse's food container

indicators.note: the jumbled colour covers the horse letters, holding them inside
ghastly suggests a horrible mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A hideous puce blanket over a horse's feed bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ghastly' makes ECUP of the colour, and 'cover for' wraps it round the nursery word for horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cup holds a boiled egg at the table, so it is a small container for food.

clue.text: Have a go dividing tree climbing shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
the attempt word splits the tree word by going inside it

parts.note: the elm is a tree
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to split a tree on which a shrub climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY goes into ELM to give ELTRYM, and 'climbing' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Browse earliest of George Ezra's work

indicators.note: only the first letter of the name is used
to work something is to manipulate it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Have a look through the early work of singer George Ezra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges EZRA to RAZE. The 's on Ezra's adds no letter; the blog calls it surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that browse feed on leaves and grass, which is what grazing means.

clue.text: Reportedly much to share out

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word for much is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a lot means much

explanation.surface: Supposedly there is plenty to go round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion, giving each person a portion.

clue.text: Try describing energy diagram and finally clarify subject

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the try word goes round the energy letter

parts.note: a go is an attempt
E is the physics symbol for energy
a graph is a kind of diagram

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A student tries to explain energy with a diagram to make things clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing round: GO goes round E to give GEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography is a school subject, the study of the earth's surface and peoples.

clue.text: Repair rig machinery, scrubbing inside — it's filthy!

indicators.note: to repair is to rework, so these letters are rearranged
scrubbing out the inside leaves only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fix the rig and clean the machine's interior, because it is dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' makes GRI, and 'scrubbing inside' empties the middle of the long word. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimy means covered in ingrained dirt, so a grimy thing is filthy.

clue.text: Disreputable men used to work in the garden

definitions.meaning: a rake is a dissolute man of loose morals

definitions.text: used to work in the garden
definitions.meaning: long-handled toothed tools for gathering leaves or levelling soil

explanation.surface: Shady men are put to work in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a libertine and a toothed gardening tool.

clue.text: Care of ladies recklessly swallowing cocaine is unsympathetic

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the drug letter inside them
acting recklessly means acting wildly, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Wild ladies in someone's care snort cocaine and become coldly heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recklessly' turns LADIES into LDASIE, and 'swallowing' puts C inside it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold as ice describes someone emotionally frozen and showing no warmth or compassion.

clue.text: Place on Kenya vacation's gone

indicators.note: in an across clue the second piece goes on after the first
vacating a word empties out its middle, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone books a holiday to Kenya, but the money has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation's' looks like a holiday, but it means Kenya emptied: KA. 'vacation's' is 'vacation is', so 'is' does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput, from German, means broken or finished, so something kaput is gone for good.

clue.text: Constable adopts bemused tone with variable efficacy

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the constable's letters hold the scrambled word

parts.note: PC stands for police constable

indicators.note: a bemused word is confused, so its letters are muddled

parts.note: in algebra y is a standard variable

explanation.surface: A puzzled policeman takes up an unpredictable manner, to good effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bemused' makes OTEN, which 'adopts' takes inside the police officer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Potency is power to produce an effect, which is what efficacy measures.

clue.text: See red, dubious about victor's merit

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the victor's letter
something dubious is doubtful or shifty, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Victor is the NATO phonetic-alphabet word for V

explanation.surface: A loser fumes about a winner who was doubtfully deserving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' turns SEE RED into DESERE, and 'about' places it around V.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, to have earned it by one's conduct.
